## Report: Marshall, "Helicobacter Connections" (Nobel lecture, 2005)

**1. The question, frozen.** The title and opening make one claim central: *what produces peptic ulcer?* It is a forward question (cause → effect). Range: human duodenal and gastric ulcers, held up to 1994, when the NIH accepted it. Contrasts it must meet: why an ulcer forms *here* and not elsewhere; why it *recurs* after healing; why some infected people never ulcerate; why the old story (acid, stress, personality, genes) seemed to fit.

**2. The explanation in parts (owner's words).** (1) a new bacterium, *Helicobacter pylori*; (2) acquired in very young children (age 2–3), faecal-oral, from family; (3) survives acid by hiding under mucus and making urease→ammonia; (4) it causes chronic gastritis; (5) that gastritis gives a lifelong susceptibility to peptic ulcer and gastric cancer; (6) acid, stress, personality and smoking are not the cause; (7) NSAIDs are a second route to gastric ulcer; (8) bismuth and antibiotics kill it and cure the ulcer.

**3. Part by part.**

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Bacterium present in ulcers | **Held** | 13 of 13 duodenal-ulcer patients carried it; killing it stops relapse. Held by the "produces the ulcer" job. |
| Acquired in early childhood | **Held if** | Held only by his own adult self-infection and Osler's child epidemics. Doubtful job: the age. Test that would settle it: follow 2–3-year-olds. |
| Faecal-oral route | **Loose** | Oral-oral fits the same data; nothing here tells them apart. Could be replaced by any close-contact route. |
| Urease/ammonia, under mucus | **Two routes** | Mucus and ammonia each help it survive acid; neither alone is needed. Urease also drives the CLOtest and C14 breath test. |
| Causes chronic gastritis | **Held** | Drinking the culture added gastritis; bismuth removed it and gastritis healed. Remove bismuth and it relapses. |
| Gastritis → lifelong ulcer | **Held** | The 1985 blinded trial: patients cured kept ulcers healed for 12 months, infected ones relapsed. |
| "Lifelong susceptibility" | **Held if** | No reading separates the carriers who ulcerate from the ~50% of carriers who do not. Needs a gauge. |
| Acid/stress/personality not the cause | **Held** | Cimetidine heals but ulcers recur; Jung scores rise when the bug is eradicated. One change (kill bug vs lower acid) tells the two apart. |
| Smoking as risk factor | **Loose** | His trial: smoking made no difference once the bug was gone. Idle to the causal claim. |
| NSAIDs → gastric ulcer, no gastritis | **Held** | Four own patients, normal histology on NSAIDs; gives the 77%-vs-100% gap its reason. |
| Bismuth kills it | **Held** | Disc test: clear zone of inhibition; predicts the Martin–Hollanders relapse curves. |
| Dollar and drug-sales figures | **Idle** | They show the stakes; they do no work in the mechanism. |
| Piglet experiment | *not a part* | A failed test; says nothing about the claim's parts. |

**4. Whole-explanation checks.**
- **Flip.** Had bismuth not cut relapse, or antibiotics failed, he says he would have been wrong — a live risk, not a second story. The claim does not cover the opposite.
- **Add a job.** The healthy carriers (58% infected, only some ulcerate) and Ito's "commensal" Japanese stomachs could have sunk it. It survives by adding the natural-history part, and the new job killed a named rival (commensal), not a repeat.
- **Direction.** Correctly forward: kill the cause and the ulcer stays healed; a relapse does not bring the bug back. Blinding stopped him reading the cause off the outcome.
- **Rival built.** The acid/stress story is the strongest rival, and the trial separates them by one change.
- **Pull.** "The bug causes ulcer" pulls against "half of carriers are well." He gives way at "susceptibility." That line is drawn with no gauge — the one joint he leaves unmeasured.
- **Patches.** The 1982 data were revised when the single bacteria-negative duodenal ulcer turned out positive on the surgical specimen. He says he checked the other direction too (that he had not over-read ulcers), so the patch was disclosed, not hidden.
- **Look inside.** The bismuth electron micrograph — "organisms exploding with dense bismuth precipitates" — looks at the workings, not just the outputs.
- **Left out.** Why only *some* infected ulcerate, and how a bug that cannot stick to intestinal-type mucosa causes a *duodenal* ulcer. Both stated openly; he flags the duodenal puzzle as unsolved.

**5. Where the parts came from.**
- **Fitted:** the 100-patient association — tuned on those 100, so it says nothing about cases it never met.
- **Built:** the causal claim, the trial, the urease test — worked out with the target in view and criticised.
- **Asserted:** the childhood timing, by analogy to his own adult illness and Osler's children; not tested here. His spontaneous cure is labelled a mystery — honestly.

**6. What would make it harder to vary.**
- Reach the duodenum: name the change that lets a bug which cannot stick to intestinal mucosa cause a duodenal ulcer, and the reading that would show it. He leaves this open.
- Give "susceptibility" a gauge: a measurement separating the carriers who ulcerate from those who do not.
- Test the childhood timing directly (follow 2–3-year-olds), not through an adult self-experiment.

**7. What this does not show.** Hard to vary is not the same as true. The 1982 association could have passed and still been chance plus confounding. Passing shows the parts are held in place, not that the cause is real. The later trials (Rauws, Graham, Hentschel) and the 1994 consensus are new claims made *after* this one.

**8. One next step.** Find the change that tells "the bacterium causes duodenal ulcer" from "the bacterium merely marks a duodenal ulcer caused otherwise" — and look at the duodenum itself, where the mechanism is thinnest.
